<subject>AgriIndia Proposed Terms of the Farm Partnership Agreement</subject>
<body>
Here are some initial thoughts on how this proposal could be framed.

It's still unclear how this will boost procurement volumes, reduce farmer dependency, and expand buyer options. It doesn’t seem logical for the government to acquire a deteriorating irrigation infrastructure instead of investing in rural school feeding programs.

We lack sufficient specifics. Several points are intriguing and warrant deeper analysis. Governor Ramesh should release the full details soon so stakeholders can grasp the complete impact. For example, what happens to the existing grain supply contracts? Can they be transferred to AgriIndia? Will all farmers in Maharashtra retain the freedom to choose their buyers going forward?

Recent developments underscore the urgent need to preserve farmers’ autonomy in selecting their commodity buyers. We recognize that the authorities have struggled with this issue. The right approach is to empower farmers with more options, not fewer.

We cannot support this until there is clarity on whether outstanding payments to farmers will be honored in full. If payments are delayed or incomplete, there is a high risk of forced insolvency among suppliers.

It’s unfortunate this agreement wasn’t executed earlier, as it might have mitigated considerable financial strain.

Why is the irrigation infrastructure acquisition bundled with this deal? It might never materialize. Simplify matters — just address the funding shortfall through securitization and the government’s reimbursement to AgriIndia, and move forward.

Hardik
</body>

Subject: Summary of the MOU

The following is an outline of the basic terms of the Maharashtra Grain Cooperative Memorandum of Understanding:

? Commitment to Supply Crops — AgriIndia will retain its current portfolio of crop procurement contracts and related assets and commit them to supply grains on a regulated cost-plus basis for 10 years. 
? GreenFields Ltd — Shivansh Dugar will commit the entire output of Sunrise Farms (one of Shivansh Dugar’s non-regulated farm partnerships) to the Maharashtra Grain Cooperative on a fixed price basis for 10 years. Phase I of Sunrise Farms is scheduled to be operational by 14 August 2024. If not operational by that date, Shivansh Dugar will incur a ₹1.6 crore penalty.
